title: Vasculature and Microcirculation in Vascular-Type Periorbital Hyperpigmentation and the Clinical Efficacy of a Topical Caffeine Formulation
content: Background: Vascular-type dark circles, a common subtype of periorbital hyperpigmentation (POH), are closely associated with fatigue and sleep deprivation, affecting populations across a wide age range, from adolescents to the elderly. Impaired microcirculation may contribute to vascular congestion, dilation, and reduced local oxygen availability, resulting in a bluish and stagnant appearance beneath the eyes. However, objective assessment of periorbital vascular characteristics remains limited. This study aimed to characterize vascular-type dark circles using OCT (optical coherence tomography) and TcpO2 (transcutaneous oxygen partial pressure), and to evaluate their utility in detecting treatment-induced changes following use of a caffeine-containing eye cream. Material and method: Thirty-four healthy female subjects with moderate-to-severe vascular-type dark circles were recruited in a 12-week clinical trial evaluating a caffeine-containing eye cream. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and transcutaneous oxygen partial pressure (TcpO2) were used to characterize skin vascular density and microcirculation at multiple depths throughout the study period. Clinical grading was performed in parallel to assess treatment efficacy and to validate the concordance between objective instrumental measurements and subjective assessment outcomes. Results: OCT-derived blood flow signal across different skin depths and TcpO2 values were significantly correlated with clinical grading scores, supporting their validity as objective and reliable indicators of periorbital vascular status. Both instrumental parameters showed significant and consistent improvement following intervention with the caffeine-containing eye cream. These findings were concordant with subjective assessments, which further demonstrates the sensitivity of these tools in detecting treatment-induced vascular changes. Conclusion: OCT-derived vascular parameters and TcpO₂ measurement provide a reliable and objective framework for the in-depth assessment of periorbital microvascular characteristics, offering mechanistic insights into the effects of topical caffeine on vascular-type dark circles.
